mainTopic: Punishing sleeping Temple guards and the value of rebuke, then how the כהן who removes the ashes is chosen, and the start of the morning Temple routine.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about the לוים guarding the בית המקדש at night: a guard caught sleeping was struck with a staff and could have his clothes burned, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says this happened to his own uncle. רבי יוחנן praises the earlier generations for punishing even sleep a person could not help. That leads to teachings on the value of rebuke: רבי says a person should love rebuke, יש אומרים say to hold on to extra faithfulness, and רבי יונתן describes the reward of one who rebukes לשם שמים. The גמרא then asks how the משנה can say both that whoever wants to remove the ashes gets up early and that a lottery decides. אביי answers that the two lines describe the times before and after the lottery תקנה. He proves this from a משנה in יומא: there was once a race up the ramp, until a כהן's leg was broken and בית דין made a lottery. רבא answers instead that both lines describe the lottery period, and rising early only makes a כהן eligible. A new משנה then describes the morning: the כהנים enter the עזרה with torches, inspect it in two groups, and the lottery winner goes alone in the dark to remove the ashes, a description that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A sleeping guard is struck and his clothes may be burned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes describing the night check. If a guard did not answer the inspector's greeting, he was clearly asleep, so the inspector struck him with his staff and was even allowed to burn his garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Peace be upon you!" If he did not answer, it was clear he was asleep. The inspector would hit him with his stick, and he even had permission to burn the guard's clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of the משנה about איש הר הבית, who walked around at night checking that each לוי guard was awake. Here the משנה tells us what happened to a guard caught sleeping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An awake guard was expected to stand up and greet the inspector. Silence showed he was asleep. The punishment had two levels: a blow with the staff, and permission to go further and burn his garment.

keyTerms.meaning: It is noticeable, it is clear
He strikes him
His staff or stick
Permission, license
His garment, his clothing

phrases.english: "Peace be upon you!"
[If he did not say it,] it was clear that he was asleep,
he would strike him with his staff.
And he had permission
to burn his garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the night inspection from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guard found asleep on duty was struck with a staff, and the inspector was allowed to burn his garment.

steps.title: People hear the noise and know a guard was caught sleeping
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes what people would say when they heard the commotion: 'What is that noise in the עזרה?' The answer: a לוי is being hit and his clothes burned because he fell asleep on his watch.
steps.simpleTranslation: And people would say, "What is that noise in the Temple courtyard?" "It is the sound of a לוי being hit and having his clothes burned, because he fell asleep on his watch."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shows that the punishment was public, so everyone in the area knew what had happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not only that the guard was punished but that it became known. The public embarrassment was part of what kept the guards alert.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple courtyard
A לוי, a member of the tribe of Levi
Is being struck, is being punished with blows
Guard duty, a watch

phrases.english: And they would say: What is that noise in the courtyard?
It is the sound of a Levite being struck
and his clothes being burned,
because he fell asleep on his watch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the public reaction to the punishment described in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The punishment of a sleeping guard was public and widely known.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: it happened to my own uncle
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב tells that his mother's brother was once found asleep on guard duty, and they burned his garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: Once they found my mother's brother asleep, and they burned his clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a personal story that shows this punishment was really carried out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the משנה gave the rule. Here a תנא gives testimony that it actually happened, and to a member of his own family. This shows the rule was enforced in practice, not just written down.

keyTerms.meaning: Once, on one occasion
My mother's brother, my uncle

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת מָצְאוּ אֶת אֲחִי אִמִּי יָשֵׁן,
phrases.english: Once they found my mother's brother sleeping,
and they burned his garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת מָצְאוּ אֶת אֲחִי אִמִּי יָשֵׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule of step 1 with a real event.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The garment of a sleeping guard really was burned, as רבי אליעזר בן יעקב testifies about his own uncle.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends by stressing that sleeping on Temple guard duty was taken very seriously, with a staff blow, burned clothes and public shame.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן praises the earlier generations for their strictness
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports that whenever רבי יוחנן reached this משנה, he said: Fortunate were the earlier generations, who punished even sleep a person could not help. All the more so would they punish wrongs that were not done under such pressure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: When רבי יוחנן came to this משנה, he would say: Fortunate are the early generations, who judged even sleep that overcame a person. How much more so would they judge things that were not caused by such sleep!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reacts to the משנה with רבי יוחנן's words of praise for how strict the earlier generations were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guard who dozes off at night is close to being forced by his body, yet he was still punished. רבי יוחנן reasons with a קל וחומר: if they were this strict about something nearly beyond a person's control, they must have been even stricter about wrongs done freely.

keyTerms.meaning: Fortunate are they, praiseworthy are they
The earlier generations
Sleep that overpowers a person against his will
They carry out judgment and punishment
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: Usually a person is not punished for something done באונס (against his will). רבי יוחנן is praising the extra strictness of the earlier generations in guarding the מקדש. He is not giving a general rule that people are always punished for אונס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מָטֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּהָא מַתְנִיתָא,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Yoḥanan reached this mishna,
he said this: Fortunate are the early generations,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ עַל אוֹנֶס שֵׁינָה עוֹשִׂין דִּין.
phrases.english: for even over sleep that overcame a person they carried out judgment.
For things not caused by unavoidable sleep,
how much more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מָטֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּהָא מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A reaction to the whole משנה about punishing sleeping guards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earlier generations punished even unavoidable sleep, so they surely punished deliberate wrongdoing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the theme of the next steps: a society where people are corrected and held to account is a praiseworthy one.

steps.title: רבי: The right path is to love rebuke
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי asking which straight path a person should choose. His answer is to love rebuke, because when rebuke exists in the world, pleasantness, goodness and blessing come and evil leaves. He brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי says: Which is the straight path a person should choose for himself? He should love rebuke. As long as there is rebuke in the world, calm comes to the world, goodness and blessing come to the world, and evil leaves the world, as it says: "But to those who rebuke shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them."
steps.whatsHappening: Following the theme of correcting people, the גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי teaches that the best way to live is to love rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי is talking about a whole way of life, not one law. He says that rebuke does more than fix one person. It brings calm, goodness and blessing to the whole world and pushes evil away. The פסוק promises delight and blessing to those who rebuke.

keyTerms.meaning: A straight, upright path in life
Words of rebuke or correction
Calm, pleasantness, contentment
Leaves, departs

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Which is the upright path
that a person should choose for himself?
He should love rebuke,
for as long as there is rebuke in the world,
pleasantness comes to the world,
goodness and blessing come to the world,
and evil departs from the world,
as it says: "But to those who rebuke shall be delight,"
"and a good blessing shall come upon them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזוֹ הִיא דֶּרֶךְ יְשָׁרָה שֶׁיָּבוֹר לוֹ הָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the guards' story to a general teaching about the value of correcting others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The upright path a person should choose is to love rebuke, which brings blessing to the world.

steps.title: Another view: Hold on to extra faithfulness
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion (יש אומרים) says that the upright path is to hold on to extra faithfulness and honesty. It brings a פסוק showing that God looks favorably on the faithful.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: He should hold on to extra faithfulness, as it says: "My eyes are on the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with Me," and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a different answer to רבי's question about which path a person should choose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said the best path is loving rebuke. The יש אומרים say it is being extra trustworthy and faithful. Their proof is a פסוק saying God's eyes are on the faithful, who get to dwell with Him.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra faithfulness and honesty
The faithful people of the land

phrases.english: And some say: He should hold on to extra faithfulness,
as it says: "My eyes are upon the faithful of the land,"
"that they may dwell with Me," and so on.
phrases.notes: תהלים 101:6. "And so on" means the rest of the פסוק continues the same idea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question asked in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Another view holds that the upright path is to keep extra faithfulness and honesty.

steps.title: One who rebukes לשם שמים earns a portion with הקדוש ברוך הוא
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני quotes רבי יונתן: anyone who rebukes his friend for the sake of Heaven earns a place in the portion of הקדוש ברוך הוא. The proof is a פסוק read as 'he who rebukes a man will be with Me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Anyone who rebukes his friend for the sake of Heaven earns the portion of הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says: "He who rebukes a man shall be after Me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the theme of rebuke and brings a teaching about the great reward of one who rebukes others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a condition here: the rebuke must be לשם שמים, for Heaven's sake, and not to put someone down. The word אחרי in the פסוק is read to mean that the rebuker stands right behind God, sharing His portion.

keyTerms.meaning: One who rebukes or corrects
For the sake of Heaven, with pure intentions
The portion of God, being close to Him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמּוֹכִיחַ אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם –
phrases.english: Anyone who rebukes his friend for the sake of Heaven

phrases.aramaic: זוֹכֶה לְחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: merits the portion of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it says: "He who rebukes a man shall be after Me."
phrases.notes: משלי 28:23. "After Me" is read as being right behind God, meaning together with Him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמּוֹכִיחַ אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the theme of rebuke from step 5 and adds the reward of the one who rebukes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who rebukes another for the sake of Heaven earns a share in the portion of הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: The rebuker also receives a thread of kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן adds a second reward: a thread of kindness is drawn over the one who rebukes. The proof comes from the end of the same פסוק: he will find more favor than one who flatters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but a thread of kindness is drawn over him, as it says: "He will find more favor than one who flatters with the tongue."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן's teaching continues with an additional reward for the one who rebukes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many people fear that rebuking others will make them disliked. The פסוק teaches the opposite: in the end, the one who rebukes finds more favor than the flatterer, and God surrounds him with kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also
A thread of kindness and grace
One who flatters, literally 'makes the tongue smooth'

steps.whatToRemember: The section moves from the strict punishment of sleeping guards to a broader message. Rebuke given לשם שמים is a great thing: it brings blessing to the world, it earns closeness to הקדוש ברוך הוא, and in the end it wins more favor than flattery.

phrases.english: And not only that, but they draw over him
a thread of kindness,
as it says: "He will find more favor than one who flatters with the tongue."
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, משלי 28:23.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁמּוֹשְׁכִין עָלָיו חוּט שֶׁל חֶסֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reward to רבי יונתן's teaching in step 7, using the rest of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thread of kindness is drawn over one who rebukes, and he finds more favor than a flatterer.

steps.title: Returning to the next lines of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the next part of the משנה so it can discuss them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he found the door locked, he knew someone was there. Then it said: whoever wants to remove the ashes from the altar, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next lines of the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first quote closes off the earlier discussion about the locked door. The second quote opens a new topic: how the priest who removes the ashes from the altar is chosen.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove the ashes from the altar (תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן), the first job of the day
And so on: the rest of the quoted line is left out

phrases.english: If he found it locked, he would know, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the bathroom door from the משנה; locked meant someone was inside.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה לִתְרוֹם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ [וְכוּ׳].
phrases.english: Whoever wants to remove the ashes from the altar, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the aggadic teachings about rebuke back to the text of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה introduces the priest who wants to remove the ashes from the altar.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The משנה first suggests that whoever is ready first removes the ashes. It then says a lottery decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה contradicts itself. First you said: whoever wants to remove the ashes gets up early and immerses before the appointed כהן arrives. That means it does not depend on a lottery. Then it teaches: let him come and join the lottery. That means it does depend on a lottery!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two lines in the same משנה seem to clash about how the priest is chosen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a lottery decided, there would be no point in rushing to immerse early, so the first line suggests first-come wins. But the next line clearly says a lottery (פייס) is held. Both cannot describe the same system.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult: a contradiction within the same source
A lottery used to assign jobs to the כהנים
The appointed כהן in charge of organizing the service
Evidently, this shows that...
Rises early and immerses in a מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not comparing two different משניות. Both lines come from the same משנה, which is why it says גופא קשיא.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ: מִי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה לִתְרוֹם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ –
phrases.english: You said: whoever wants to remove the ashes from the altar
rises early and immerses
before the appointed one comes.
Evidently, the matter does not depend on a lottery.
And then it teaches: let him come and join the lottery.
Evidently, the matter does depend on a lottery!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the משנה about choosing who removes the ashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rising early implies first-come wins, but the later line says a lottery decides. Both cannot be true together.

steps.title: אביי: two time periods, before and after the תקנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the first line describes the practice before the lottery was enacted, and the second line describes the practice after.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is not difficult. Here, it describes the time before the תקנה. There, it describes the time after the תקנה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying the two lines describe two different eras.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally, whoever got there first did the job, so rising early made sense. Later the חכמים made a תקנה requiring a lottery. The משנה records both stages, so the two lines do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: introduces a resolution
An enactment of the חכמים that changes practice
Before / after

phrases.english: אביי said: it is not difficult.
Here, it is before the enactment.
phrases.notes: This is the line about rising early and immersing first.

phrases.english: There, it is after the enactment.
phrases.notes: This is the line about the lottery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two lines into two time periods
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both lines describe one single system, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: First-come applied before the תקנה; the lottery applied after it.

steps.title: Proof from יומא: the old race and the switch to a lottery
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in יומא shows there really was an earlier first-come system: a race up the ramp, with a lottery only for ties.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: at first, whoever wanted to remove the ashes from the altar did so. When there were many, they ran up the ramp, and whoever got within four אמות first won. If two were tied, the appointed כהן said to them: raise your fingers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove אביי's claim that there once was a system without a lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בראשונה, at first, shows the practice later changed, which supports אביי's 'before the תקנה.' In the old system a race decided, and fingers were counted only if two כהנים tied.

keyTerms.meaning: At first: signals an earlier practice that was later changed
The ramp leading up to the altar
Four cubits, the finish zone at the top of the ramp
Won the right to do the job
Raise your fingers, to be counted in a lottery

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the משנה can preserve older Temple practices alongside newer ones, which is how אביי's answer works.

phrases.english: As we learned: at first,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִתְרוֹם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, תּוֹרֵם.
phrases.english: whoever wants to remove the ashes from the altar removes them.
When there are many of them,
they run and go up the ramp.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַקּוֹדֵם אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ בְּתוֹךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת – זָכָה.
phrases.english: Whoever gets ahead of his fellow within four cubits wins.
phrases.notes: He means within four cubits of the top: whoever reaches that zone first wins.

phrases.english: If two were tied,
the appointed one says to them: "Raise your fingers."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer with a source.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that there was a time before the lottery תקנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in יומא 22a describing the earlier race up the ramp

steps.title: How the fingers were raised for the lottery
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה explains that each כהן raises one or two fingers, and a thumb is not used in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what do they hold out? One or two fingers. And they do not hold out a thumb in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה continues by explaining exactly how the finger-counting lottery worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It adds the practical details of the lottery: a כהן may raise one or two fingers, but never a thumb. This rounds off the description of how the job was assigned.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold out (fingers to be counted)
Thumb

phrases.english: And what do they hold out?
One or two fingers.
And they do not hold out a thumb in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה with details of the lottery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the lottery each כהן raises one or two fingers, and a thumb is not used in the מקדש.

steps.title: The ramp accident that led to the lottery
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in יומא ends by telling why the lottery was made: two כהנים tied in the race, one pushed the other, and his leg broke. בית דין then ruled that removing the ashes is done only by lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once two כהנים were tied, running up the ramp. One pushed the other, and his leg broke. When בית דין saw that people were coming into danger, they made a rule that removing the ashes would be done only by lottery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה in יומא. That משנה explains how the race system changed into a lottery system.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes אביי's proof. There really was a time before the lottery, when a race decided who removed the ashes. The lottery was a later rule, made because the race became dangerous. So it fits to say one line of our משנה describes the old way and another line describes the new way.

keyTerms.meaning: Pushed
Danger
The court (here, the authorities over the מקדש)
They made a rule (enacted a תקנה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a rabbinic rule (תקנה) changing how the מקדש service was assigned, to protect the כהנים from harm.

phrases.english: There was an incident: two were equal,
running and going up the ramp,
and one of them pushed the other,
and his leg was broken.
phrases.notes: This is the leg of the כהן who got pushed.

phrases.english: And when the court saw
that they were coming into danger,

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ תּוֹרְמִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: they made a rule that they would not remove the ashes from the altar
except by lottery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה in יומא from Steps 12–13. It finishes the story of how the lottery replaced the race.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's answer that our משנה describes two time periods, before and after the lottery rule
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in יומא, which tells how an accident on the ramp led בית דין to make the lottery rule

steps.title: Both lines describe the time after the lottery rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the contradiction differently. Both lines of the משנה describe the time after the lottery rule. Getting up early and immersing only makes a כהן eligible to join the lottery before the ממונה arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: both lines describe the time after the rule. This is what the משנה means: whoever wants to come and join the lottery gets up early and immerses before the ממונה arrives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the contradiction from Step 10. He disagrees with אביי's 'before and after' approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the first line, 'whoever wants to remove the ashes gets up early,' describes the old race system. רבא says there is no need for two time periods. Getting up early and immersing is simply how a כהן gets into the lottery, so both lines fit the same system.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that (both lines)
After the rule was made
Gets up early
Immerses in a מקוה
The כהן appointed to run the lottery

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. אביי says the lines describe two time periods: the race first, then the lottery. רבא says both lines describe the lottery period, and getting up early only qualifies a כהן to take part in the lottery.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not deny that there once was a race. He only says our משנה does not need it to explain its two lines.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לְאַחַר תַּקָּנָה,
phrases.english: Rava said: Both this and that are after the rule,
and this is what it teaches:
whoever wants to come and join the lottery
gets up early and immerses
before the appointed one arrives.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לְאַחַר תַּקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's answer and its proof, רבא offers a different way to settle the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the first line so that both lines describe the same time period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first line seems to describe a first-come system, which clashes with the lottery.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first line only describes how a כהן gets ready to join the lottery, so there is no clash.

steps.title: The ממונה opens the small door and the כהנים enter the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. The ממונה takes the key, opens the small door, and goes from the בית המוקד into the עזרה. The כהנים follow him, holding two torches.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took the key and opened the small door. He went from the Chamber of the Hearth into the courtyard. The כהנים went in after him, holding two burning torches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the next משנה. It continues describing the morning routine in the מקדש step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before dawn, the כהנים are inside the בית המוקד. The ממונה uses the key to open the small door into the עזרה. It is still dark, so they carry torches to light the way.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Key
A small door set in or beside a large gate
The Chamber of the Hearth, where the כהנים slept
The מקדש courtyard
Torches

phrases.english: MISHNA: He took the key
phrases.notes: "He" is the ממונה, the כהן in charge.

phrases.english: and opened the small door,
and went from the Chamber of the Hearth into the courtyard,
and the priests went in after him,
with two burning torches in their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָטַל אֶת הַמַּפְתֵּחַ וּפָתַח אֶת הַפִּשְׁפָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion of the previous משנה ends, and a new משנה begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ממונה opens the small door, and the כהנים follow him into the עזרה carrying torches.

steps.title: Two groups check the courtyard and meet at the place of the חביתים
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים split into two groups, one going east and one going west along the covered walkway. They check as they go until they meet at the place of the חביתים maker. Both groups say 'all is well,' and the חביתים maker is set to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: They split into two groups. One group walked along the covered walkway toward the east, and the other toward the west. They kept checking as they walked until they reached the place of the griddle-cake maker. When they got there, both groups said: 'Peace, all is well.' Then they set the griddle-cake maker to make the griddle-cakes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It describes the כהנים checking the courtyard and then starting the first preparation of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group goes around the courtyard in a different direction, so the whole area gets checked. When they meet, they confirm to each other that everything is in order. Only after this check does the work begin, starting with the חביתים.

keyTerms.meaning: Groups
A covered walkway (portico) around the courtyard
Checking, inspecting
The כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering
The כהן who prepares the חביתים

phrases.english: They split into two groups:
these walk along the covered walkway toward the east,
and those walk along the covered walkway toward the west.
They would keep checking as they went
until they reached the place of the griddle-cake maker.
phrases.notes: The חביתים are the כהן גדול's daily flour offering, fried on a griddle.

phrases.english: When they arrived, both groups said:
"Peace, all is well."
They set the griddle-cake maker to make the griddle-cakes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה. After entering the courtyard, the כהנים check it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two groups check the courtyard from opposite directions, meet and confirm that all is well, and then the חביתים preparation begins.

steps.title: The lottery winner removes the ashes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that the כהן who won the lottery for תרומת הדשן is the one who performs it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever won the right to remove the ashes from the מזבח is the one who removes them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from the lottery to the actual job. The winner of the lottery now does תרומת הדשן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps explained why a lottery was set up: a race once led to an injury. Now the משנה shows the result in practice. Only the winner does this service, and nobody else.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a portion of the ashes from the top of the מזבח, the first service of the day
Won (the lottery), earned the right
To lift off or remove (the ashes)

phrases.english: The one who won the right to remove the ashes from the altar,
he shall remove them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁזָּכָה לִתְרוֹם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, הוּא יִתְרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the morning. After the lottery and the inspection, the winner begins his job.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the כהן who won the lottery performs תרומת הדשן.

steps.title: The other כהנים remind him to wash and tell him where the coal pan is
steps.stepSummary: The other כהנים warn the winner not to touch the vessel before washing his hands and feet at the כיור. They also remind him where the מחתה is kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: The others tell him: be careful not to touch the vessel until you wash your hands and feet from the כיור. The coal pan is in the corner between the ramp and the מזבח, on the west side of the ramp.
steps.whatsHappening: The other כהנים give the winner two reminders before he starts. First wash at the כיור, then find the מחתה in its set place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may not do any service before קידוש ידים ורגלים, so they warn him not even to touch the vessel before washing. They also tell him exactly where the מחתה is, because he will be going up in the dark.

keyTerms.meaning: Washing the hands and feet, which a כהן must do before any service
The basin in the עזרה used for this washing
Coal pan, used to scoop up the ashes
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Corner

phrases.english: And they say to him:
Be careful that you do not touch the vessel

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתְּקַדֵּשׁ יָדֶיךָ וְרַגְלֶיךָ מִן הַכִּיּוֹר.
phrases.english: until you sanctify your hands and your feet from the basin.
And the coal pan is placed in the corner
between the ramp and the altar,
on the western side of the ramp.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵם אוֹמְרִים: הֱוֵי זָהִיר שֶׁלֹּא תִּגַּע בַּכְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the reminders given to the winner named in Step 18 before he begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן may not touch the service vessel before washing his hands and feet from the כיור. The מחתה is kept in the corner west of the ramp, between it and the מזבח.

steps.title: He goes in alone, with no lamp, by the light of the altar fire
steps.stepSummary: No one goes in with the כהן, and he carries no lamp. He walks by the light of the wood fire on the מזבח, and the others cannot see him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nobody goes in with him, and he has no lamp in his hand. He walks by the light of the fire on the מזבח. The others would not see him...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the כהן walking alone in the dark to do his job. The last line starts a new sentence that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scene shows him going alone: no companion and no lamp. The only light comes from the מערכה, the wood fire burning on the מזבח. The line 'they would not see him' begins a new point that the משנה finishes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The arranged pile of burning wood on the מזבח
Lamp
Walks

steps.confusionAlert: The last phrase, 'they would not see him,' is not the end of the thought. The משנה continues it in the next lines.

phrases.english: No person enters with him.
And there is no lamp in his hand,
rather, he walks by the light of the arrangement of wood.
They would not see him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the reminders in Step 19, the משנה describes how the כהן actually walks up to do the service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן doing תרומת הדשן goes alone, without a lamp, lit only by the fire on the מזבח, out of the other כהנים' sight.
